name: SSC

levels.note: 10th pass. Age 18–25 (MTS), 18–23 (GD). Physical standards for GD.
12th pass. Typing test: 35 wpm English / 30 wpm Hindi. Age 18–27.
Any degree. JE needs B.E./B.Tech. Age 18–30 (CGL), 20–25 (CPO).

stages.name: Tier 1 (CBT)
stages.tests: 100 Qs, 60 min. Reasoning, GK, Quant, English. 200 marks.
stages.note: Qualifying. Negative marking 0.50. Cut-off varies by post and category.

stages.name: Tier 2 (CBT)
stages.tests: 200 Qs, 2 hrs. Quant, English, GK, Reasoning. + Computer (qualifying).
stages.note: Merit prepared from Tier 2. Descriptive paper (essay + letter) for some posts.

stages.name: Skill Test / Typing
stages.tests: Typing: 35 wpm English / 30 wpm Hindi (10 min). DEST for DEO.
stages.note: Qualifying only. No marks added to merit.

stages.name: Document Verification
stages.tests: All originals, caste, domicile, NOC, gap certificate.
stages.note: Any discrepancy = rejection. Verify before applying.

syllabus.exam: Tier 1 — CGL and CHSL (Computer Based Examination)
syllabus.pattern: 100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes. Negative marking 0.50 per wrong answer. Section-wise split is published in the notice; the syllabus below is common to both.

topics.items: Analogies, similarities and differences, space visualisation, problem solving, analysis, judgement, decision making, visual memory, discrimination, observation, arithmetical reasoning, verbal and figure classification, non-verbal series, coding-decoding, statement-conclusion, syllogistic reasoning

Whole numbers, decimals, fractions, percentage, ratio and proportion, square roots, averages, interest, profit and loss, discount, partnership, mixture, time and distance, time and work, basic algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, height and distance, data interpretation, charts and graphs
India and its neighbouring countries, history, culture, geography, economic scene, general polity, Indian constitution, scientific developments, current affairs

Spot the error, fill in the blanks, synonyms and antonyms, spelling correction, idioms and phrases, one word substitution, active and passive voice, direct and indirect narration, cloze passage, reading comprehension, sentence improvement, shuffling of sentence parts, sentence rearrangement

syllabus.books: SSC CGL Tier 1 Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: Objective papers held in sessions as published in the notice, with negative marking. A descriptive paper (essay and letter) is qualifying for some posts.

topics.items: Arithmetic at higher difficulty, advanced mensuration, geometry, trigonometry, surds and indices, statistics, data interpretation, charts and tables
Higher-difficulty puzzles, seating arrangement, blood relations, syllogism, coding-decoding, data sufficiency
Vocabulary, grammar and usage, error spotting, cloze test, reading comprehension, para jumbles, sentence rearrangement
Deeper current affairs, history and culture, polity and constitution, economy, science and technology, environment, computers
Computer basics, MS Office, operating systems, networking, internet and email — qualifying

syllabus.books: SSC CGL Tier 2 Guide (Amazon)

syllabus.pattern: Typing: 35 wpm English or 30 wpm Hindi in 10 minutes. Data Entry Speed Test (DEST) for DEO posts. Both qualifying.

topics.items: Speed and accuracy only — no syllabus text is tested

prepPlan.phase: Start the notice is out — Months 1–2
prepPlan.what: Give one diagnostic Tier 1 mock cold on day one. That tells you which of the four sections costs you the most marks. Start with that section for the first month; do not spend equal time on all four.
Finish English grammar and vocabulary (the highest-scoring, lowest-cost section), then reasoning type by type. Do 50 arithmetic questions daily — SSC is mostly speed maths, not advanced maths.
Two Tier 1 mocks a week and one Tier 2 section test. Review every wrong answer by writing it in an error notebook. Target 45 seconds per question.
If the exam calendar puts Tier 2 soon after Tier 1, start Tier 2 preparation in parallel from month 3. Tier 2 is where final merit is decided — Tier 1 only filters.
Full mocks at the actual slot, error notebook revision, and 10 minutes of typing practice daily for the skill test. Do not open new books.

reality: SSC CGL is the most popular government exam. 20-30 lakh applicants for 7000-15000 vacancies.
Tier 1 is qualifying but the cut-off is high. Focus on accuracy, not just speed.
CHSL and CGL have different syllabi. CHSL is easier but fewer vacancies.
GD Constable has physical tests (running, long jump, high jump). Start fitness early.
SSC exams have a fixed calendar. CGL in Aug-Sep, CHSL in Mar-Apr, MTS in Sep-Oct.
Job posting: Income Tax (CBDT) and Customs (CBIC) are most sought after in CGL.

faq.q: What is the difference between SSC CGL and SSC CHSL?
faq.a: CGL = Combined Graduate Level (graduate posts: Inspector, Auditor, ASO). CHSL = Combined Higher Secondary Level (12th pass posts: Clerk, DEO, PA). Different eligibility, different exams.

faq.q: Can a 12th pass apply for SSC CGL?
faq.a: No. CGL requires graduation. 12th pass can apply for CHSL, MTS, GD Constable, and Stenographer.

faq.q: What is the age limit for SSC exams?
faq.a: MTS: 18-25 years. CHSL: 18-27 years. CGL: 18-30 years (varies by post). CPO: 20-25 years. GD Constable: 18-23 years. Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.
No attempt limit for SSC exams (age-based). You can apply as long as you meet the age criteria.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in SSC exams?
faq.a: Yes. Tier 1: 0.50 per wrong answer. Tier 2: 0.25 per wrong answer (varies by paper). No negative marking in skill test or typing.

faq.q: Where do I find official SSC notifications?
faq.a: ssc.gov.in (main site) and regional SSC websites. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification PDF on every listing page.
